prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce a ubiquitin ligase to ubiquitinate and destroy a chosen protein through a ternary complex, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of glue degraders.

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as the whole prize, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The shared principle is a small molecule that induces a ternary complex between an E3 ligase and a target, so that destruction is catalytic and event-driven instead of occupancy-based. That principle is supported by structures, cooperativity and kinetics, it reaches targets without conventional pockets, and it has been reproduced widely. The Chair asks whether the PROTAC and glue strands can be one achievement. I think they can, because cereblon recruitment is the same ligase-target proximity mechanism, and Handa's identification of cereblon is the piece that explains drugs already in patients. On the Medicine question raised by Brzezinski, the citation should name the chemical principle (induced proximity in a ternary complex, small-molecule design of ligase recruitment) and not a clinical outcome, which is the emphasis I have written into it. I do not treat clinical approval as a precondition, since the chemical mechanism is settled and independently confirmed.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, so a 2026 award rests on concept, mechanism and early clinical signals. The three-name limit excludes Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL ligands made degrader design rational, as well as Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and the PROTAC and glue lineages have separate histories, so a combined citation could be read as a compromise between two prizes. A committee could also fairly say this is medicinal chemistry and pharmacology that Medicine might claim. Finally, a mature and cleanly attributed prize such as Car-Parrinello would avoid all of these attribution and timing problems.

responses.point: Aqvist now supports B020 but wants Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a citation limited to bifunctional degraders, and would accept Handa in place of Deshaies only with a two-modality citation.
responses.response: This is the argument that held me longest, because my opening ballot named Ciulli and I still believe his VHL ligands and ternary-complex work were what turned the concept into design. I have still stayed with Handa for two reasons. Ciulli's contribution extends a modality that Crews and Deshaies had already defined, whereas cereblon is an independent discovery that gives the glue half of the field its mechanism. And a PROTAC-only citation leaves out the part that is already in patients. I do not accept dropping Deshaies for Handa, since the 2001 concept should anchor the prize, and I accept that omitting Ciulli is a real cost the citation language should not hide.

responses.point: Chabes proposes two parts, Liu alone for base editing plus Crews and Deshaies for heterobifunctional degraders, and stops at two degrader names to avoid choosing a third.
responses.response: I accept that Liu alone is the right attribution for B047 and that deamination without strand cleavage is a different chemical principle from nuclease cutting, so I do not use the 2020 prize as an argument against it. Where I differ is on structure. Leaving the third degrader seat empty does not resolve the glue question, it only avoids it, and it leaves a part that excludes the cereblon discovery. Combining two young, therapeutic-adjacent fields also strikes me as presentist when one part already has full committee traction. I rank B047 as my first alternative and would support it as a second part only if B020 attribution could not be settled.

responses.point: Somfai holds that Buchwald and Hartwig C-N coupling should be first, as mature and cleanly attributed, with degraders somewhat premature without approvals.
responses.response: Cleanness of attribution is a real strength and I do not dismiss the prematurity concern. My difficulty is that C-N coupling extends the theme recognised in 2010, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work complicates the priority story. The Chemistry prize has not required drug approval when the chemical principle is established, and the ligase-target ternary-complex principle is established by structures and independent groups. Brzezinski's point that lenalidomide-class glues are already established drugs also weakens the claim that the principle itself is early.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved to B020 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa but warns that it could be claimed as Medicine, that the two strands may look like a forced merger, and that nitrogenase attribution is harder than degraders.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution and with his remark that I should not make the prize wait for a PROTAC approval. On the Medicine concern, I think the right answer is in how the citation is written: the achievement is the design of small molecules that induce ligase-target proximity, a question of binding, cooperativity and ternary-complex structure, and not the development of a drug. I also appreciate his candour that nitrogenase attribution is harder, which is why I keep it out of my configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Handa over Ciulli for the third seat, and whether a single citation can span PROTAC and glue lineages without seeming to dismiss Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC drug will be judged to make 2026 premature relative to a mature candidate such as B061.
I rely on general knowledge for priority dates of the 2001 PROTAC work and the cereblon identification, and have not verified them.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or any other credited name on B020, B047 or B061. My only link is a field-level interest in peptide and nanoparticle self-assembly (relevant to B010 and B024, neither in my configuration), which does not require recusal. I note Sparr's disclosure on B010 and B024 and Brzezinski's on B028 and see no reason for any recusal affecting B020.
